desc: Fresh seafood served Western, Asian and Japanese style. The menu runs the gamut from fish & chips to poke bowls and $300 seafood platters, but it's all quite tasty and very popular, so book ahead on weekends.

name: Ocean Restaurant
desc: Easily the flashiest restaurant in Sentosa, built inside the SEA Aquarium so that diners face directly into the enormous "Open Ocean" tank showcasing manta rays and countless tropical fish. Set menus only (4 to 8 courses

name: The Cliff
desc: In sight of jungle, beach and sea, repeatedly voted the most romantic restaurant in Singapore and popular with bosses out for a naughty night with their secretaries. Book a table on the lower deck for the best views.

name: Rumours Beach Club
desc: The restaurant is pleasant but slightly overpriced and the outdoor seating is very nicely set up, although the volume is often cranked up way too high. Reserve in advance if you want one of the little pavilions.

name: Tanjong Beach Club
desc: Standing proudly apart on Tanjong Beach, this is the top beach club on Sentosa and priced to match. Maritime French Riviera vibes, brunchy food menu, boozy cocktails. Reserve ahead, particularly on weekends. Various dayb

name: Coastes
desc: The very first beach bar when coming in from Beach Station is a pleasant enough place to get your feet in the sand while sipping on a glass of cold white wine. Seating runs right up to the water's edge and the vaguely Au

name: FOC Sentosa
desc: Barcelona meets Singapore at this beach bar with paellas and a tasty if pricy tapas menu. Set quite far back from the water's edge, but it's also quieter than the rest since it stands some way apart at the east end of Pa

name: Ola Beach Club
desc: This family-friendly Hawaiian-inspired beach club stands out for having its own pool (free for customers) and an array of watersports options (charges apply). The food is pretty dire, but the beer is cold and the tiki co

name: Restoran Selera Sambal
desc: Ayam penyet.

name: Tanjung Langsat Food Court
addr: Jalan Ipil 1, Kawasan Perindustrian Tanjung Langsat
desc: Food court.

name: Bora Bora Botanist
addr: Unit No.1 Block B, Senibong Cove, Masai, 81750
desc: Restaurant.

name: Kedai Makan Rahmat
desc: Famous for their deep fried fish, or siakap goreng, which are fried with their scales on, keeping the flesh inside tender. The restaurant is built on top of stilts extending over the shore of the Johor Straits.

name: Rowan & Parsley
addr: No. 17, Jalan Cenderai 20, Kawasan Perindustrial Kota Putri, Masai, 81
desc: Smokehouse barbecue restaurant in a garden-themed venue.

name: Coffeetrap Restaurant
desc: A sidewalk alfresco dining outlet with live music from early as 7:30PM. The best dishes are lamb shank, grilled salmon, chicken chop with gravy. Popular with locals and expatriates F-M from early as noon and Tu-Th from 3

name: Todak (Orang Asli) Restaurant
desc: Set on a breezy wooden boardwalk right on the Straits of Johor, the restaurant is famous for its seafood and crab platters. The tables are moodily lit with red lights, covered with red plastic and matched with red chairs

name: 328 Katong Laksa
desc: This was one of the combatants of the "laksa wars" of yore. Now franchised all over Singapore, but this is the original, still supervised by the owner. Do try the otah (spicy fish paste).

name: Marine Parade Laksa
desc: Run by the people who originally ran #49, although some think the quality has gone down (see Zhen Shan Mei in [[Singapore/North and West#Hawker centres

name: Chuan Kee Satay
hours: 6PM until sold out around 10PM, closed M & Th, Su
desc: Satay freshly grilled and served with peanut sauce. Extremely long wait, so order the pork satay first and then look for other things to eat.

name: Mattar Road Seafood BBQ
desc: One of the few places where you can order crab and still have money to spend elsewhere. They're famous for their chilli crabs, but the white pepper crab is something different to try.

name: Whitley Road Big Prawn Noodle
desc: Exactly as it says, big prawn noodles, although the number of prawns depends on the size of the bowl ordered. All that flavoursome soup comes from prawn heads.

name: Kampong Rojak
desc: Rojak with sweet dark sauce, quality prawn paste and generous portions of cucumber, pineapple and you tiao (dough fritters).

name: Leng Heng BBQ Seafood & Claypot Deluxe
desc: A Makansutra legend, their black pepper crabs are fiery and not for the faint hearted. They have giant prawns fresh from the sea and the BBQ stingray is yummy as well.

name: Musa Ikan Bakar Stall
desc: There are at least ten satay stalls here with not much difference between them. Musa's thick and chunky peanut satay sauce stands out though, cooked by the owners.

name: International Muslim Food
desc: This nondescript stall has a neverending queue for Singapore's best nasi lemak, Malay-style coconut rice with fried chicken, chili, egg and various goodies. Quite honestly, it's not that different from what you'll get el

name: Guan Hoe Soon Restaurant
desc: One of Singapore's most popular Peranakan restaurants, serving distinctive Peranakan dishes such as ayam buah keluak, chicken with keluak nuts, and babi pongteh, a pork stew.

name: Kim Choo
desc: Housed in an old Peranakan shophouse, Singaporeans know this shop best for its Peranakan-style rice dumplings (nyonya chang), but they've opened up their second story for visitors and also operate a Peranakan restaurant

name: He Ping Restaurant
desc: Serves excellent claypot chicken rice, cooked over a charcoal fire. All freshly made to order, this can cause lengthy queues during the busy weekends.

name: Lion City Frog Leg Porridge
desc: Famous for their (spicy) Gong Bao frog leg porridge. You can also order some of the beef kway teow from the stall on the opposite side of the street and they'll bring it to your table.

name: Quentin's The Eurasian Restaurant
desc: One of the few restaurants in Singapore serving the distinctive cuisine of the Eurasian community. Some of their signature dishes include devil's curry, shepherd's pie and sugee cake.

name: Jumbo Seafood
desc: Best known for its chilli crabs. Other outlets at Riverside Point (opposite Clarke Quay), Serangoon Gardens, Changi, and Riverwalk, but this is the original.

name: Little Red House
desc: Another chilli crab joint.

name: Long Beach Seafood Restaurant
desc: Known for a wide variety of seafood including black pepper crab and butter crayfish and one of the most crowded seafood restaurants in the East Coast area on weekends. One should also try the duck they serve, which is pr

name: The Mango Tree
desc: Offers Kerala-style Indian seafood in a tastefully decorated restaurant, quite unlike the raucous Chinese places above. Plenty of vegetarian options too.

name: No Signboard Seafood
desc: Started as a tiny hawker stall too poor to afford a signboard, now franchised across the island with, inevitably, large neon signboards proclaiming "No Signboard". Known for white pepper and butter crabs.

name: Sin Huat Seafood
desc: Looks very unassuming, but the crab bee hoon stewed in rice noodles is legendary. Cooked to order, so expect to wait up to an hour and expect "legendary" service as well: they won't serve you if you are eating duck rice

name: Georges Mad Bar and Cafe
desc: Laid back and cosy ambience with a good range of beers and spirits. The pub food is average.

name: Next Door Cafe
desc: A European-style cafe perfect for pizzas, sandwiches and salads. Also offers a wide range of alcoholic & soft drinks. Books, magazines and board games also available. Perfect place to chill out for lunch and dinner.

name: Vic's Wine Bar
desc: A great place to unwind, meet friends and enjoy excellent wine from Vic's own Australian vineyards.

name: Vie Cafe
desc: Wide selection of wines, whiskeys, beers and other spirits.

name: Anjappar
desc: Indian cuisine with focus in southern Indian, especially the Chennai region.

name: Heavenly Wang
desc: Be here for a quick Singapore style breakfast such as Kopi & Teh, kaya toast, and soft-boiled eggs, or something more substantial like Nasi Lemak or chicken congee.

name: Penang Culture
desc: Savor the street food favorites from the Malaysian island town, such as nasi lemak, fried kway teow (rice vermicelli), or prawn noodle soup in a fine-dining setting.

name: Staff Canteen
desc: Featuring a wide array of local food at local prices, this miniature hawker centre is where the airport staff eat. Best of all, it's also open to the public, albeit a little hidden & with a slightly higher price.

name: Terrace Chinese Kitchen
desc: Dim sum and other Chinese stir-fried dishes.

name: TGM & Root 98
desc: Choice of Japanese or Korean specialties and vegetarian under one roof. The set menu is a deal worth trying.

name: Crave
desc: Taste the famous Adam Road Nasi Lemak (coconut rice) that you can pay per ingredient, and pair it with Teh Tarik (milk tea)

name: Food Gallery
desc: The food court offering diverse Singaporean delicacies.

name: Ippudo Express
desc: Head here for a quick ramen stop with various toppings from the famous Japanese chain.

name: O'Learys Sports Bar
desc: Premium diner style dishes and drinks from the bar to enjoy while catching up with the ongoing sport matches on screen.

name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast
desc: The famous Singapore Kopitiam franchise with its renowned toast with kaya jam, or try it together with a bowl of soft boiled egg and a cup of coffee.

name: Jinjja Kitchen
desc: Korean style fried chicken and other assorted Korean delights such as kimchi fried rice, Korean-style pasta, and stew.

name: Jones the Grocer
desc: Coffee shop from Australia featuring warm coffee and cold smoothies. Snacks range from pastries and sandwiches to fruit cups and salads.

name: XW Western Grill
desc: Flame grilled chicken, steak, and fish, accompanied with a free flow of salad from the self-service bar.

name: Chutney Mary
desc: Craving the authentic Indian spices? Head here for either a light street snack or a more substantial thali set.

name: Kaveri Indian Vegetarian
desc: One of the few vegetarian friendly restaurants at the airport. Specialises in southern Indian flavours.

name: Straits Food Village
desc: A food court offering assorted dishes from Singapore in a rustic wood atmosphere. Order the food by selecting from the kiosk and pick up your meal from the restaurant when your number is called.

name: The Satay Club by Harry's
desc: Primarily Malay and Indonesian favorites such as satay (grilled skewered meats), nasi goreng (fried rice), gado-gado (salad with peanut sauce), and deep-fried kueh. Grill section also expansive with kushi-yaki style skew

name: 4 Fingers Curry Chicken
desc: Crispy chicken that is good on its own or mixed with seafood for more protein, or rice for a more balanced meal. Can be enjoyed à la carte or with a combo of drinks & fries.

name: Curry Times
desc: Owned by the famous curry puff vendor Old Chang Kee, with its signature dishes such as curry chicken, fish fillet rice, prata, curry bun, and classic Singapore desserts.

name: Kopitiam
desc: Food court serving local dishes at reasonable prices (by airport standards).

name: Paradise Dynasty
desc: A cavernous Chinese restaurant with mainly dishes made for sharing. Its specialty dish, xiao long bao (steamed dumpling filled with meat and soup) is worth to try.

name: Mr. Teh Tarik
desc: The pulled milk tea (Teh Tarik) is not to be missed. There are also something more substantial such as assorted roti prata or roti john flavors, briyani rice, and fried noodle or rice.

name: Swensen's
desc: Serves diner-style breakfast and snacks, steaks, pastas and pizzas, and of course, ice cream.

name: LeNu Chef Wai's Noodle Bar
desc: In mood for something warm and hearty? Head here to savor its noodle with a choice of beef or pork broth, simmered for at least 12 hours resulting in rich flavor and high protein content, or congee with toppings you can

name: The Kitchen by Wolfgang Puck
desc: Enjoy breakfast in the morning or steak, pasta, and pizza in the afternoon and evening, with recipes tailored by the renowned chef.

name: Singapore Food Street
desc: A 1960s-themed food court offering culinary delights from the island nation.

name: Ma Mum
desc: Halal-certified laksa, chicken rice, and noodle soups, some with a touch of Thai spiciness.

name: Old Street Bak Kut Teh
desc: Specializing in one of Singapore's favorite delicacies, pork ribs herbal soup (Bak Kut Teh). Also provides comfort food such as congee & pork noodle.

name: International Food Hall
desc: Food court offering a diverse range of dishes from all over the world.

name: Tiger Den
desc: Enjoy Singapore's very own beer, tapped up to a pitcher or bottled.

name: Crystal Jade GO
price: Set menus $14-20. Dim sum $5-8, Main cou
desc: An extensive selection of dim sum in addition to noodles and congees. Look for its set menu which for a cheaper price makes a complete meal.

name: Burger & Lobster
desc: Beef burgers & assorted lobster platters, whole or as a sushi roll.

name: Food Republic
desc: Want to eat but not limited to a specific restaurant? The food court at level B2 serves a wide range of options, from local highlights to international choices.

name: Poulet Bijou
desc: Modern French bistro featuring soups, pot pies & its signature roast chicken with a choice of diane, mushroom cream, or cranberry sauce.

name: Shang Social
desc: Dim sum for lunch or authentic dishes from mainland China all day.

name: Tonito Latin American Kitchen
desc: Classic tapas, Mexican light bites, Peruvian stews, and Argentinian pastas

name: Violet Oon
desc: Peranakan-style cuisine, from satays, pratas, rendang, to sweet desserts. Special vegan menu also available.

name: The World is Flat
desc: A former staple for alcoholic drinks at Terminal 1, the bar at its new location still serves draft beer & zesty cocktail mixes. For something more substantial, enjoy filling burgers and hearty sandwiches, or donburi (Jap

name: Birds of Paradise
desc: Premium ice cream with a local twist, such as the bestseller white chrysanthemum, sea salt hojicha, coconut, spiced pear, pandan, and lemongrass.
